title: Mathematical models for understanding genetic diversity of the new coronavirus
author: Pierre Teodosio Felix
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bmbvk2n6
materials: Molecular Variance Analysis (AMOVA) and Genetic Distance

steps.title: Measure Genetic and Molecular Diversity
steps.instruction: Quantify the genetic diversity and molecular indices of the studied groups using standard indices.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the standard index of genetic diversity (H) following Nei (1987) or the method by Pons and Petit (1995) to measure expected heterozygosity.
Obtain molecular diversity indices by calculating the average number of paired differences as described by Tajima (1993), specifically for sequences not fitting the neutral theory model.

steps.title: Estimate Site Frequency Spectrum (SFS)
steps.instruction: Perform a local frequency spectrum analytical test (SFS) on DNA sequence data to estimate demographic parameters.

substeps.instruction: Run simulations using fastsimcoal2 software.

steps.title: Calculate Theta Population Parameters
steps.instruction: Qualify genetic diversity using various Theta estimators.

substeps.instruction: Estimate Theta Hom to determine expected homozygosity in a population in equilibrium between drift and mutation.
Calculate Theta (S) (Watterson, 1975), Theta (K) (Ewens, 1972), and Theta (π) (Tajima, 1983).

steps.title: Analyze Mismatch Distribution
steps.instruction: Perform mismatch distribution analysis to establish population demographic behavior patterns by relating the observed number of differences between haplotype pairs.

steps.title: Model Demographic and Spatial Expansion
steps.instruction: Apply expansion models based on the observed population behavior.

substeps.instruction: For Pure Demographic Expansion: Estimate the probability of differences between two non-recombined, randomly chosen haplotypes in a haploid population that reached momentary balance after τ generations (sizes 0N to 1N).

For Spatial Expansion: Use this model if the population was initially restricted to a small area and shows growth over a short time. Account for: L (number of loci), Gamma Correction (for non-uniform mutation rates), nd (substitutions between two sequences), ns (transitions), nv (transversions), ω (G + C ratio), Paired Difference (number of different loci), and Percentage difference.

steps.title: Perform Haplotypic Inferences
steps.instruction: Estimate haplotype frequencies for data with unknown gametic phase.

substeps.instruction: For haplotypic/genotypic data: Estimate frequency (^pi) by observing the relationship between haplotype i and xi times its number of copies.
For genotypic data with unknown gametic phase: Use the maximum likelihood method or the expected Maximization (MS) algorithm.

steps.title: Calculate Corrected Haplotype Differences
steps.instruction: Apply nucleotide substitution models to estimate the corrected percentage of difference between two haplotypes.

substeps.instruction: Jukes and Cantor Method: Assume identical replacement rates for A, C, G, and T to correct for multiple substitutions per site.
Kimura Two-Parameter Method: Correct for multiple site substitutions while accounting for different replacement rates between transitions and transversions.
Tamura Method: Extend the Kimura 2-parameter method by calculating transition-transversion relationships and general nucleotide frequencies from original data.
Tajima and Nei Method: Apply an extension of the Jukes and Cantor method using original data.
Tamura and Nei Model: Infer different rates of transversions and transitions, distinguishing transition rates between purines and pyrimidines.

steps.title: Estimate Distances Between Haplotypes
steps.instruction: Determine the distance between haplotypes based on the data source.

substeps.instruction: For RFLP-produced haplotypes: Verify the number of paired differences by scouting the number of different alleles.
For Microsatellite-produced haplotypes: Perform a simple count of different alleles and use the sum of the square of the differences of repeated sites (Slatkin, 1995).

steps.title: Construct Minimum Spanning Network (MSN)
steps.instruction: Calculate the distance between operational taxonomic units (OTU) from the paired distance matrix of haplotypes.

substeps.instruction: Use the MINSPNET.EXE software (running in DOS) to generate the MSN tree based on a modification of the Rohlf (1973) algorithm.

steps.title: Estimate Frequencies for Unknown Gametic Phase
steps.instruction: Use specialized algorithms for multilocal data where gametic phase is unknown (phenotypic data).

substeps.instruction: EM Algorithm: Use a maximum likelihood model that maximizes expected values to obtain estimates from multilocal data.
ELB Algorithm: Reconstruct the unknown gametic phase of multilocal genotypes by adjusting sizes and locations of neighboring loci to explore rare recombination.

steps.title: Perform Neutrality Tests
steps.instruction: Test the hypothesis of selective neutrality and population balance.

substeps.instruction: Ewens-Watterson homozygosis test: Summarize allelic frequency distribution (limited to sample sizes ≤ 2,000 genes and ≤ 1,000 alleles).
Accurate Ewens-Watterson-Slatkin Test: Compare probabilities of random samples with observed samples.
Chakraborty's test of population amalgamation: Calculate the observed probability of a randomly neutral sample with a number of alleles ≥ observed, based on the infinite allele model.
Tajima Selective Neutrality Test: Use for short DNA sequences or RFLP haplotypes, commuting two estimators using theta mutation as a parameter.
FS FU Test of Selective Neutrality: Use for short DNA sequences or RFLP haplotypes to assess the observed probability of a randomly neutral sample with alleles ≤ observed value using estimator θ.

steps.title: Measure Interpopulation Diversity
steps.instruction: Analyze the genetic structure and variance between populations.

substeps.instruction: Molecular Variance Analysis (AMOVA): Divide total variance into covariance components to measure intra-individual, interindividual, and interpopulation differences.
Locus-by-locus AMOVA: Perform analysis for each locus separately at the haplotypic level to estimate variance components and f statistics.
Paired Genetic Distances: Generate paired F ST parameters to estimate short-term genetic distances, applying algorithmic adaptation to linearize distance with divergence time.
Reynolds Distance: Measure divergence of pairs of fixed N-size haplotypes over t generations based on F ST indices.
Slatkin's linearized F ST's: Estimate divergence of two Haploid populations of N size that diverged t generations ago and remained isolated.
Nei's average number of differences: Calculate the increase in genetic distance between populations based on gross (D) and liquid (AD) differences.

Relative population sizes analysis: Estimate divergence time between populations of unequal sizes (Gaggiotti and Excoffier, 2000) assuming a pure fission model from an ancestral population of N0 size.
Accurate population differentiation tests: Use an analog of Fisher's exact test (extended to rxk contingency table) to test random distribution of k haplotypes/genotypes among r populations.
Assignment of individual genotypes: Determine the origin of specific individuals using a list of potential source populations and estimated allelic frequencies.
Detection of loci under selection: Use F-statistics (adapted from Cavalli-Sforza 1996/Lewontin and Krakauer 1973) to identify natural selection effects.

description: The specific methodologies for paired F ST estimators, Molecular Variance (AMOVA), Genetic Distance, mismatch, demographic and spatial expansion analyses, molecular diversity and evolutionary divergence time were obtained using 20,000 random permutations.
